subtopics.title: IoT and the Arduino board
subtopics.theory_md:
**IoT** is a network of physical objects (things) with sensors, actuators and connectivity that collect and exchange data over the Internet with little human help. Layers: **sensing** (sensors), **processing** (microcontroller), **communication** (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet), **cloud/application**. Examples: smart home, smart agriculture, wearables.

**Arduino** is an open-source board built around a microcontroller (Uno: **ATmega328P**, 16 MHz, 5 V). Uno has **14 digital pins** (D0-D13, 6 of them PWM), **6 analog inputs** (A0-A5), 32 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM, USB port, power jack, reset button. Programs are called **sketches**, written in the **Arduino IDE** (C/C++) and uploaded through USB using the bootloader.
subtopics.basics_md: A thing becomes 'smart' when it can sense something, think a little, and talk to the Internet. Arduino is the small cheap computer that does the sensing and thinking.
key_points: IoT = sensors + microcontroller + connectivity + cloud, objects exchanging data over the Internet
Arduino Uno: ATmega328P, 14 digital pins (6 PWM), 6 analog inputs, 5 V, 16 MHz
Program is a sketch written in Arduino IDE and uploaded via USB

**Building blocks**
1. Sensors and actuators (sense and act)
2. Microcontroller such as Arduino (processing)
3. Communication (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet)
4. Cloud and application (storage, analysis, user interface)

questions.q: Describe the Arduino Uno board: its microcontroller, pins, memory and how a program is loaded.
questions.model_answer_md:
1. **Microcontroller:** ATmega328P, 8-bit, 16 MHz, operating at 5 V.
2. **Pins:** 14 digital I/O (D0-D13), of which 6 give PWM (3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11); 6 analog inputs (A0-A5).
3. **Memory:** 32 KB flash (program), 2 KB SRAM, 1 KB EEPROM.
4. **Loading:** the sketch is written in the Arduino IDE, compiled, and uploaded through the USB port using the bootloader. USB also powers the board.
points: 14 digital pins with 6 PWM, 6 analog inputs
Sketch uploaded from Arduino IDE over USB

subtopics.title: Analog input, PWM and Serial
subtopics.theory_md:
**analogRead(A0)** uses the Uno's **10-bit ADC**: 0 to 5 V maps to 0-1023, so $V=\text{reading}\times 5/1023$ and resolution is $5/1023\approx4.89$ mV.

**analogWrite(pin, 0-255)** gives **PWM** on pins 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11 (8-bit). Duty cycle $=\text{value}/255$, average voltage $=5\times\text{duty}$. It controls LED brightness or motor speed.

**Serial:** `Serial.begin(9600)` in setup (baud rate), `Serial.println(x)` prints to the Serial Monitor over USB.

Typical sensors: LDR and thermistor (analog), DHT11 temperature/humidity (digital), PIR motion, ultrasonic HC-SR04 (distance). Actuators: LED, buzzer, servo, relay.
subtopics.basics_md: Digital pins know only on or off. Analog input measures a voltage as a number. PWM fakes an in-between voltage by switching on and off very fast.
key_points: Duty cycle = value/255; average V = 5 x duty
Serial.begin(9600) and Serial.println for the monitor
Sensors give input, actuators act on output

questions.model_answer_md:
Duty $=\dfrac{128}{255}\times100=50.2\%$

Average voltage $=5\times\dfrac{128}{255}=2.51\ \text{V}$ (about half of 5 V, so the LED is at half brightness).
